**UK open banking crosses one billion payments as VRPs drive growth**

*Open Banking Limited reports the ecosystem has passed one billion cumulative payments and 100 billion API calls, with variable recurring payments now the primary growth engine as single domestic payments decline.*

The UK open banking ecosystem has surpassed one billion payments, according to Open Banking Limited, the entity overseeing CMA9 bank compliance. The milestone is accompanied by 100 billion cumulative API calls, reflecting both payment initiation and data-sharing activity across the ecosystem.

The composition of that growth is shifting. Single domestic payments fell 1.2% month on month, while variable recurring payments (VRPs) rose 6.7% over the same period. That divergence suggests the initial use case that drove open banking adoption, one-off account-to-account transfers, may be plateauing, with recurring payment mandates becoming the more dynamic segment. VRP growth aligns with the commercial VRP frameworks now being rolled out through the UK Payments Initiative and individual providers.

The billion-payment figure is cumulative rather than annualised, so it measures adoption history rather than current throughput. For context, UK card payments numbered 31.4bn in 2024. Open banking payments remain a small fraction of total UK payment volumes, but the rate of acceleration, and the shift toward VRPs, matters more than the headline number for those building commercial propositions on these rails.

*Sources: [Open Banking Reaches 1 Billion Payment Milestone in the UK](https://www.pymnts.com/news/banking/2026/open-banking-reaches-1-billion-payment-milestone-in-the-uk/) — PYMNTS.com | [UK Open Banking Hits Landmark One Billion Payments and 100 Billion API Calls](https://ffnews.com/news/uk-open-banking-hits-landmark-one-billion-payments-and-100-billion-api-calls) — Ffnews | [UK Open Banking hits one billion payments milestone](https://www.finextra.com/pressarticle/110503/uk-open-banking-hits-one-billion-payments-milestone?utm_medium=rssfinextra&utm_source=finextrafeed) — Finextra Research | [UK Open Banking ecosystem surpasses one billion payments and 100 billion API calls](https://www.openbankingexpo.com/news/uk-open-banking-ecosystem-surpasses-one-billion-payments-and-100-billion-api-calls/) — Openbankingexpo | [Open banking surpasses one billion payments](https://www.uktech.news/fintech/open-banking-surpasses-one-billion-payments-20260728) — UKTN | [Open Banking passes one billion payments milestone](https://www.credit-connect.co.uk/news/open-banking-passes-one-billion-payments-milestone/) — Credit Connect*

**Visa cuts 2,600 jobs as it restructures for AI-driven operations**

*The payments network is eliminating 7% of its workforce, with technology and product roles bearing the heaviest losses as it redirects investment toward AI capabilities.*

Visa is cutting approximately 2,600 positions, representing 7% of its global workforce, with technology and product teams most affected. The restructuring is framed as a reconfiguration for what the company describes as the AI era, shifting resources away from legacy technology functions toward automation and AI-driven product development.

The cuts come during a period of heavy AI investment across the payments industry. Visa has launched an agentic payments programme in Europe, partnered with OpenAI, and built a threat intelligence platform — all within the past year. Reducing headcount in traditional technology roles while scaling AI capabilities is consistent with that direction, though the scale of cuts suggests cost discipline is also a factor.

Even the largest incumbents are now compressing their technology organisations rather than simply adding AI on top. Payment processors and banks building their own AI strategies should expect similar workforce rebalancing across the industry as automation reshapes how payments technology is built and maintained.

*Sources: [Tech jobs go as Visa cuts workforce by 7%](https://www.finextra.com/newsarticle/48161/tech-jobs-go-as-visa-cuts-workforce-by-7?utm_medium=rssfinextra&utm_source=finextrafeed) — Finextra*

**PayPoint reports steady open banking revenue as merchant services dip**

*First-quarter results show PayPoint's open banking and digital payments division growing 4.1% while merchant services and Love2shop declined, underscoring uneven performance across the group's payment lines.*

PayPoint reported first-quarter results showing its digital payments and open banking division generated £3.2 million in revenue, up 4.1% year on year from £3.1 million. Nick Wiles, PayPoint's chief executive, pointed to a growing pipeline of new business in the segment. Merchant services fell 6.1% to £7.7 million, while the Love2shop voucher business dropped 10.3% to £7.0 million.

The divergence across PayPoint's divisions reflects a pattern visible elsewhere in UK payments: open banking-adjacent revenue streams are growing modestly but consistently, while traditional merchant acquiring faces pricing and volume pressure. PayPoint's open banking revenues remain small in absolute terms, but the segment is now the only one of the group's three main divisions posting growth.

PayPoint completed its acquisition of AperiData in June, giving it additional capabilities in open banking. Access PaySuite separately acquired Ordo's open banking infrastructure on June 17, adding request-to-pay and payment initiation capabilities. The real test for PayPoint's open banking ambitions is whether the AperiData deal accelerates growth in subsequent quarters.

*Sources: [1st Quarter Results](https://www.globenewswire.com/news-release/2026/07/29/3334974/0/en/1st-quarter-results.html) — GlobeNewswire | [1st Quarter Results](https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/stocks/articles/1st-quarter-results-060000068.html) — Yahoo Finance*

**Nexi posts steady first-quarter growth with open banking contributing to digital segment**

*Nexi's digital banking and open banking segment now represents 11% of group revenues, with open banking and SEPA clearing volumes among the drivers lifting the unit in the first quarter of 2026.*

Nexi's first-quarter 2026 results show its digital banking and open banking segment contributing 11% of group revenues, with growth driven by SEPA clearing volumes, open banking services, network infrastructure and PagoPA bill payment processing. The company reported steady overall growth and strong cash generation despite what it described as macroeconomic headwinds.

Continued speculation about Nexi's ownership structure adds a strategic dimension to these results. Italy's state lender Cassa Depositi e Prestiti is reportedly considering increasing its stake, and private equity firms are circling the company. How Nexi allocates investment between its merchant acquiring business and its digital infrastructure operations, including open banking, will be shaped partly by whichever ownership configuration prevails.

For the broader European market, Nexi's open banking revenues illustrate that processor-scale economics are beginning to flow through open banking rails, even if the segment remains a minority contributor. As SEPA instant payments mandates take full effect, processors with established clearing infrastructure stand to benefit disproportionately.

*Sources: [Nexi H1 2026 slides: steady growth, strong cash amid macro headwinds](https://www.investing.com/news/company-news/nexi-h1-2026-slides-steady-growth-strong-cash-amid-macro-headwinds-93CH-4818743) — Investing.com*
